claim_verdicts.source: flutter analyze / flutter test on scratch copy of examples/don-hang @ stage-1 DonHang.App (round 1)

claim_verdicts.evidence: StatelessWidget doc: UI 'does not depend on anything other than the configuration information in the object itself and the [BuildContext] in which the widget is inflated.' ListTile doc: 'Requires one of its ancestors to be a [Material] widget.'; build asserts debugCheckHasMaterial. Scaffold is not itself a Material but builds one (scaffold.dart:3236 'child: Material('). Lesson generalises to 'Material widgets such as ListTile' (not all do, e.g. CircularProgressIndicator) and calls Scaffold 'a Material widget'.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A widget still gets its `BuildContext` from where it is placed, and some Material widgets, such as `ListTile`, need a `Material` widget above them, which `Scaffold` provides, but everything specific to one use arrives through the constructor.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Opinion/framing carried from design.l1.solid-srp and outline items 1-2. Round-1 overreach ('everything the widget depends on', 'nothing else reaches it') is gone: §3 now says 'the values anyone using it must give it' and §4 acknowledges BuildContext and the Material ancestor. Consistent with best-practices.md: 'Split them into different widgets based on encapsulation but also on how they change'.

best-practices.md: 'When `setState()` is called on a `State` object, all descendent widgets rebuild. Therefore, localize the `setState()` call to the part of the subtree whose UI actually needs to change.' setState doc: 'it causes the widget to rebuild, possibly triggering rebuilds for the entire subtree rooted at this widget'. Supports both 'rebuilds only that widget's subtree' and 'the smaller the widget, the less each change touches'.

ListView.builder doc: 'the builder is called only for those children that are actually visible' and 'The `itemBuilder` callback will be called only with indices greater than or equal to zero and less than `itemCount`.' The ledger text ('as rows are needed') is right, but the lesson sentence drops the condition: 'calling `itemBuilder` once for each of the `itemCount` products' is false for off-screen rows, and a row scrolled back into view is built again.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `ListView.builder` builds the list, calling `itemBuilder` with an index below `itemCount` each time it needs the row for one product:

issues.text: Lesson text is stronger than claim 9 and than the docs. ListView.builder: 'the builder is called only for those children that are actually visible'; indices are only 0..itemCount-1. It is not called once per product: off-screen rows are not built, and rows are rebuilt when scrolled back.
issues.quote: calling `itemBuilder` once for each of the `itemCount` products
issues.fix: Replace the sentence with: "`ListView.builder` builds the list, calling `itemBuilder` with an index below `itemCount` each time it needs the row for one product:" (keep the colon before the code block). Update the vi translation to match.

issues.text: Overgeneralised. Only some Material widgets require a Material ancestor (ListTile doc: 'Requires one of its ancestors to be a [Material] widget'); Scaffold is not itself a Material but builds one inside.
issues.quote: Material widgets such as `ListTile` expect a Material widget like `Scaffold` above them
issues.fix: Change to: "some Material widgets, such as `ListTile`, need a `Material` widget above them, which `Scaffold` provides".

issues.text: Keys are correct. But explanations say the row can be used 'anywhere', which contradicts §4 of the revised lesson (ListTile needs a Material widget above it). Same overreach in q4 option b explanation.
issues.quote: a small contract lets it be used anywhere.
issues.fix: q3 correct (en): replace "a small contract lets it be used anywhere" with "a small contract lets it be used on any screen that has a product"; (vi): "hợp đồng nhỏ giúp nó dùng được ở mọi màn hình có sản phẩm". q4 b (en): "with just a `Product` it fits any screen that has one"; (vi): "chỉ với một `Product` thì màn hình nào có sản phẩm cũng dùng được".

issues.text: This paragraph jumps: no example in the lesson shows a small widget holding its own state, and 'When one of them changes' is ambiguous (its code changes, or its state?). Summary line 5 rests on this paragraph, so I cannot reconstruct why extracting keeps state 'in the right place'.

issues.fix: Replace 'one of them' with a concrete case in one sentence, e.g. "If the product screen calls `setState`, only its subtree rebuilds; `ProductTile` holds no state, so reading it needs no knowledge of the screen's loading."
